title: Kali Fractal
description: Grow a glowing fractal from one line of math. The starter already picks c, drifts it slowly, tone-maps the result and darkens the corners; you write three parts. First, Kali's fold: mirror p into the first quadrant, invert it through the unit circle, and shift it by c. Second, a cosine palette. Third, the orbit trap: fold p again and again, and after each fold measure its distance to a trap shape made of two shapes joined together. Wherever a fold lands near the trap, add a glow, colored by which fold it was. Open "Stuck? Show the numbers" on any part for the fold count, the trap and the palette. c circles once every 14 seconds, so the fractal keeps changing shape.
hintText: Start with one fold and a plain trap: color = vec3(exp(-24.0 * abs(length(p) - 0.5))) after a single kaliFold should show soft rings. Then loop. Joining two shapes is min() of their distances, the same union you used on the combining board.
